# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

- Customer portal (`app/dashboard/**`) and admin ops portal (`app/admin/**`) are separate sidebar apps sharing `components/portal/Shell.tsx` (sidebar, topbar, notifications bell, ⌘K command palette backed by `/api/search`).
- Design system lives in `app/globals.css` (glass cards, gradient buttons, navy palette) + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` + `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free SVG charts). Use these — do not add chart libraries.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id).
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.
- Wallet amounts are integer cents.

## Documentation — keep it current (required)

- **Every change, fix, or addition MUST update `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` in the same commit.** Add a dated bullet to §15 (Change history) and edit any section the change affects (data model, subsystems, feature catalog, integrations, roadmap, etc.). A commit that changes behaviour without touching the docs is incomplete.
- Keep `ROADMAP.md` in sync too: check off / move the item you completed.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` is the single source of truth. The public mirror at `https://revsports.ca/docs` is regenerated from it with `node scripts/publish-docs.mjs` (zero-dep markdown→styled-HTML renderer → `/var/www/nxeon-docs/index.html`) — run that after editing the doc so the hosted page matches. The `/docs` nginx location lives in `scripts/configure-domains.sh` so it survives vhost regeneration.
- The claude.ai artifact webpage (`https://claude.ai/code/artifact/9b0c97f5-4c34-4f89-bee9-b5a80eb23892`) can only be updated from an interactive Claude Code session (headless/cron runs can't reach it) — that refresh is best-effort, the repo doc + `/docs` page are authoritative.

## Commands

- Build: `npm run build` (must pass before restarting services)
- Deploy after changes: `npm run build && systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker`
- Worker logs: `journalctl -u nxeon-worker -f`
- E2E test: `npx tsx scripts/e2e-test.ts` (orders a real VM; delete it afterwards via a DELETE job)
- Admin credentials: `/root/nxeon-credentials.txt`

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. It regenerates nginx vhosts, obtains Let's Encrypt certs, updates APP_URL in both `.env`s, and restarts web. That's the whole migration.
- **Routing**: customer portal on `https://BASE_DOMAIN` (admin path returns 404 here — hidden); admin ops portal on `https://ADMIN_HOST` (secret subdomain, root 302→/admin); staging on `https://STAGING_HOST`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP.
- Secure cookies are on (`COOKIE_SECURE=1`) now that real HTTPS exists. Stripe webhook is live at `https://BASE_DOMAIN/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Environments

- **Production**: `/opt/nxeon`, DB `nxeon`, services `nxeon-web` (port 3000) + `nxeon-worker`, nginx port 80, VPS pools IP 10.20.0.100–250 / SSH ports 20000–29999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD`. Public: http://51.79.162.96
- **Staging**: `/opt/nxeon-staging`, DB `nxeon_staging`, services `nxeon-staging-web` (port 3001) + `nxeon-staging-worker`, nginx port 8080, ISOLATED VPS pools IP 10.20.0.50–99 / SSH ports 30000–30999, NAT chain `NXEON_FWD_STG`, VM tag `nxeon-staging`. Public: http://51.79.162.96:8080. Admin creds: `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt`.
- Instance differences are driven entirely by `.env` (NXEON_ENV, NXEON_COOKIE_NAME, NXEON_NAT_CHAIN, NXEON_TAG, NXEON_IP_START/END, NXEON_SSH_PORT_START/END, NXEON_CRED_FILE, PORT, APP_URL) — the code is identical.
- **Deploy flow**: push to GitHub → `scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` builds+migrates+restarts staging → verify at :8080 → `scripts/promote-production.sh` rebuilds+restarts production. The improvement agent should test changes on staging before promoting.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

From the actions-volumes file, I can see there's an `ownedVolume` check that validates the volume belongs to the current user.

Looking deeper, `attachVolume` validates server ownership, and `detachVolume` relies on the volume being owned since the serverId comes from the database. But `deleteVolume` is a critical issue — it only has a client-side confirmation via `window.confirm` with no server-side verification string, making it directly callable as a destructive server action. Even worse, there's no status check preventing deletion of attached volumes, and no verification that the server is stopped before removing the disk. This means a volume can be deleted while still mounted on a running VM, which could cause data corruption if Proxmox allows hot-unplug on SCSI devices with hotplug enabled. The `detachVolume` function has similar gaps in its validation. I'm seeing a critical issue in `volumeAttach`: when `diskName` is null due to a race condition and the volume previously had data, it creates a fresh empty disk instead of reattaching the existing one, silently orphaning the customer's data. There's also a potential edge case where if a Server row somehow had a VMID in the 9000-9999 range, it could bypass guards, though that's probably not reachable in practice.

Now looking at `volumeDelete` — it matches any config key whose volid equals `volume.diskName`, and if that diskName somehow equaled the OS disk's volid, it would delete the root disk. The question is whether that's reachable: `diskName` comes from either the slot read-back or the "appeared" diff, and `freeScsiSlot` skips scsi0, so normally it shouldn't be possible. But if the read-back races or if the appeared-diff logic has a gap...

Actually, there's a concrete scenario: two concurrent VOLUME_ATTACH jobs could cause issues, though one in-flight job per server is supposed to be enforced. The real concern is `keyForVolid` matching — it iterates all config keys looking for one with a matching volid. Also worth noting that `volidOf` strips at the first comma, so `"vmdata:vm-101-disk-0,size=50G"` becomes just `"vmdata:vm-101-disk-0"`, and special disks like the EFI or cloudinit drive won't match `isRealVolid` since they don't follow the vm-\d+-disk-\d+ pattern. But `keyForVolid` could still find the first matching key...

The dangerous part is that both `volumeDetach` and `volumeDelete` check `key.startsWith("scsi")` without explicitly excluding `scsi0`, so if `Volume.diskName` somehow contains the root disk's volid, detaching that volume would unplug the VM's root disk, and deleting it would destroy it. The question is how `diskName` could end up holding the root volid in the first place — that would have to come from `volumeAttach`.

I'm considering whether a stale config snapshot during the initial attach could be missing `scsi0`, but that seems unlikely. More plausible is something happening during VM migration or reinstall. I need to search for other places where `diskName` gets written and check the reinstall guards, plus look at what the worker's resize handler does with disk sizing during downgrades.

Looking at `lib/resize.ts`, the `resizeQuote` function blocks disk shrinking in the upgrade path, and `applyResize` doesn't verify ownership — which is concerning since it's called both from the authenticated resize endpoint and from an unauthenticated Stripe confirmation route. I need to verify that the Stripe route actually validates the session and that the serverId in the metadata belongs to the user who paid. Then I should check `ResizeDown.tsx` and the `resizeServerDown` function to see if the client-side filtering of disk shrinks is enforced server-side, since that's a critical security boundary.

# Data-destruction audit — /opt/nxeon volumes & disk paths

Read in full: `lib/actions-volumes.ts`, `worker/volumes.ts`, `components/customer/Volumes.tsx`, `lib/resize.ts`, `components/customer/ResizeDown.tsx`, `lib/disk-expand.ts`, `worker/disk-expand.ts`, `lib/extra-disk.ts`, `lib/actions-disk.ts`. Plus the paths they reach into: `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts` (`resizeServerDown`, `reinstallToOs`), `worker/index.ts` (`resize`, `remove`, `reinstall`, `destroyVm`, job loop), `worker/product-renewals.ts` (unpaid-volume sweep), `app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts`, `lib/auth.ts`, `prisma/schema.prisma`.

---

## Answers to the six questions, per destructive operation

| Operation | 1. Server-side confirm? | 2. Ownership? | 3. Target scoped to resource? | 4. Silent shrink? | 5. Server row loaded? | 6. VMID 9000–9999 guard? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Volume **detach** | **NO** — client `window.confirm` only | YES (`ownedVolume`) | YES (`volume.serverId` from DB, not input) | n/a | YES (`volume.server` include) | **NO** |
| Volume **delete** | **NO** — client `window.confirm` only | YES (`ownedVolume`) | YES | n/a | YES | **NO** |
| Volume **format/mkfs** | n/a — **no mkfs exists in these paths** (SOLID) | — | — | — | — | — |
| Disk **resize DOWN / shrink** | n/a — **blocked in 4 layers** (SOLID) | YES | YES | **NO — cannot shrink at all** | YES | **NO** |
| Extra disk **delete** | n/a — **no shrink/decrement path exists** (SOLID) | — | — | — | — | — |
| (adjacent) **reinstall** = full wipe | **NO** — client-only "type ERASE" | YES | YES | n/a | YES | **NO** |

---

## FINDINGS

### F1 — HIGH — `deleteVolume` permanently destroys customer data with no server-side confirmation, no state guard, no rate limit

`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-volumes.ts:167`

```ts
export async function deleteVolume(volumeId: string): Promise<{ error?: string }> {
  const { user, volume } = await ownedVolume(volumeId);
  if (volume.status === "DELETING") return { error: "Volume is already being deleted." };
```

That `DELETING` check is the **entire** set of preconditions. The confirmation is client-side only:

`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/Volumes.tsx:120`
```ts
if (confirmMsg && !window.confirm(confirmMsg)) return;
```
`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/Volumes.tsx:186-188` supplies the "This permanently destroys its data and cannot be undone" string — which never reaches the server. Server actions are directly POST-able by id.

**Failure scenario:** a signed-in customer (or any script running in their session — a malicious browser extension, a stored-XSS payload on the dashboard, a mis-fired retry) POSTs the `deleteVolume` action with `["<volumeId>"]`. No dialog, no typed name. → `VOLUME_DELETE` job → `/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:279` `await conn.post(\`/nodes/${conn.node}/qemu/${server.vmid}/config\`, { delete: key });` destroys the ZFS zvol → `/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:287` `await db.volume.delete(...)` removes the only record. There is no backup of volume disks anywhere in this codebase. **Unrecoverable.**

Two aggravators on the same function:
- **No `DETACHED` requirement.** An `ATTACHED`, mounted, actively-written volume can be deleted. The worker hot-unplugs it first (`worker/volumes.ts:273`) then destroys it.
- **No rate limit and no `assertNotImpersonating()`.** Compare `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-disk.ts:25-26` (`MAX_EXPANDS_PER_WINDOW = 5`) and `:42` (`await assertNotImpersonating();`) — the *non-destructive* growth path is strictly better defended than the *irreversible destruction* path.

### F2 — HIGH — `detachVolume` hot-unplugs a mounted disk from a RUNNING VM

`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-volumes.ts:147-154` — the only guard is `volume.status !== "ATTACHED"`. There is **no `server.status` check**, which is conspicuous because `attachVolume` *does* have one at `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-volumes.ts:124`:
```ts
if (!server.vmid || server.status !== "RUNNING") {
```

Worker: `/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:235-237`
```ts
if (key && key.startsWith("scsi")) {
  await conn.post(`/nodes/${conn.node}/qemu/${server.vmid}/config`, { delete: key });
}
```
Proxmox's default `hotplug` is `disk,network,usb`, and provision (`/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:284-303`) never sets `hotplug`, so this is a **live SCSI hot-unplug**. No `fsfreeze`, no `sync`, no guest-agent `umount`, no power-off requirement.

**Failure scenario:** customer has the volume mounted at `/var/lib/mysql` on a running VM. They click "Detach" — the client dialog at `components/customer/Volumes.tsx:173` literally reassures them *"Data is preserved."* The device vanishes mid-write → ext4 aborts the journal / goes read-only → InnoDB corruption. On re-attach the filesystem needs `fsck` and recent transactions are gone.

Same primitive fires **without any human at all** from billing: `/opt/nxeon/worker/product-renewals.ts:434`
```ts
data: { type: "VOLUME_DETACH", serverId: volume.serverId, payload: { volumeId: volume.id } },
```
An overdue invoice yanks a mounted disk out of a running production database.

### F3 — HIGH — `scsi0` (the root disk) is not excluded from detach/delete

`/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:235` and `/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:272` both use:
```ts
if (key && key.startsWith("scsi")) {
```
`"scsi0".startsWith("scsi")` is **true**. And `/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:278-280`:
```ts
// Deleting an "unused" entry destroys the underlying disk.
if (key) {
  await conn.post(`/nodes/${conn.node}/qemu/${server.vmid}/config`, { delete: key });
}
```
— no key filter at all on the second pass.

The only thing preventing a customer's OS disk from being destroyed by a "Delete volume" click is that `Volume.diskName` never happens to hold `scsi0`'s volid. But `diskName` is not read from a reliable source — it comes from a three-tier heuristic at `/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:181-194`, whose third tier is a **set difference across two Proxmox config reads that this very file documents as racy** (`worker/volumes.ts:172-175`: *"Proxmox applies a config POST ASYNCHRONOUSLY — an immediate GET can still return the pre-write view… That race is exactly how volumes ended up with a null diskName"*).

**Failure scenario:** any transient config-read state where the "appeared" diff resolves to exactly one volid and that volid is `vm-<vmid>-disk-0` → `Volume.diskName = "vmdata:vm-101-disk-0"`. The customer then clicks Delete on that volume → `keyForVolid` returns `"scsi0"` → the OS disk is detached then destroyed. The server is gone, and `db.volume.delete` erases the audit trail of which disk was targeted.

Missing one-liner: `if (key === "scsi0") throw new Error("refusing to touch the root disk");` at both call sites. Also missing: an assertion that `key.startsWith("unused")` before the destroy pass.

### F4 — HIGH — re-attach with a null `diskName` silently orphans the data and hands back a blank disk

`/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:166`
```ts
const source = volume.diskName ? volume.diskName : `${storage}:${volume.sizeGB}`;
```
There is no check for "this volume was attached before but we lost its volid". `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:432-436` confirms null-`diskName` ATTACHED volumes exist in production:
```ts
const realAttached = attachedVolumes.filter(
  (v) => !(typeof v.diskName === "string" && v.diskName.startsWith("sandbox:"))
);
```

**Failure scenario:** Volume `V` (500 GB) holds a customer's data; `V.diskName` is null from the documented race. Customer clicks Detach → `worker/volumes.ts:231` `if (server?.vmid && volume.diskName)` is **false**, so nothing is unplugged, but `:240` still flips the row to `DETACHED` and `:242-248` notifies *"The volume and its data are preserved."* Customer clicks Attach → line 166 creates a **brand-new empty `vmdata:500` disk**, and `:199` overwrites `diskName` with the new volid. The customer sees an unformatted 500 GB disk and their data is on an orphaned zvol with zero DB references. A later Delete destroys the new empty disk and leaks the real one forever.

### F5 — MEDIUM — `volumeDetach` reports success when it did nothing, weakening the reinstall purge guard

`/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:231-248`: the Proxmox block is conditional on `server?.vmid && volume.diskName`, but `:240` `await db.volume.update({ where: { id: volume.id }, data: { status: "DETACHED" } });` is unconditional.

The worker's reinstall guard only blocks on status:
`/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:428-430`
```ts
const attachedVolumes = await db.volume.findMany({
  where: { serverId: server.id, status: "ATTACHED" },
});
```
A physically-present-but-falsely-`DETACHED` volume passes it. Then `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:448` → `destroyVm` → `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:357-360`:
```ts
const delUpid = await conn.del(`/nodes/${conn.node}/qemu/${vmid}`, {
  "destroy-unreferenced-disks": 1,
  purge: 1,
});
```
→ the volume's disk is purged with the VM.

What actually saves this today is the stricter *action-level* guard at `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:112-117`, which counts by `serverId` regardless of status. That means the last line of defence lives in the web layer, not the worker — the inverse of where you want it.

### F6 — MEDIUM — full-wipe reinstall has no server-side confirmation either

`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:81-84`
```ts
export async function reinstallToOs(
  serverId: string,
  osTemplateId: string
): Promise<{ error?: string }> {
```
No confirm parameter. The "type ERASE" gate is client-only: `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/ReinstallOs.tsx:39` `const confirmed = confirmText.trim().toUpperCase() === "ERASE";`. Admin equivalent is also client-only: `/opt/nxeon/components/admin/ServerAdminActions.tsx:52` `disabled={pending || confirmText !== hostname}`.

**Failure scenario:** a direct POST of `reinstallToOs(["<serverId>", "<anyActiveOsTemplateId>"])` destroys and re-clones the VM (`worker/index.ts:448`, `purge: 1`). Every byte gone, no confirmation ever required.

### F7 — MEDIUM — no VMID 9000–9999 guard anywhere (violates CLAUDE.md "NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999")

The **only** `9000` comparison in the entire codebase is a display filter: `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/monitoring/page.tsx:244` `const orphan = !rec && v.vmid < 9000;`.

Every destructive call site takes `vmid` straight from the DB with no range check:
- `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:357` — `conn.del(\`/nodes/${conn.node}/qemu/${vmid}\`, { "destroy-unreferenced-disks": 1, purge: 1 })`
- `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:308` and `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:581` — `conn.put(\`.../qemu/${vmid}/resize\`, { disk: "scsi0", size: ... })`
- `/opt/nxeon/worker/disk-expand.ts:344` — `conn.put(\`.../qemu/${server.vmid}/resize\`, ...)`
- `/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:167`, `:236`, `:273`, `:279` — config writes and deletes

`Server.vmid` is `Int?` with no range constraint (`prisma/schema.prisma:296`), and allocation is `/opt/nxeon/lib/proxmox.ts:109-111` `return Number(await req("GET", "/cluster/nextid"));` — unconstrained. Any DB fix-up, VM-adoption flow, or import that lands a template vmid on a `Server` row turns a customer's "Delete volume" click into destruction of the Ubuntu 24.04 template. Add an `assertCustomerVmid(vmid)` at the top of `destroyVm`, both `resize` paths, and the three `volumes.ts` config mutators.

### F8 — MEDIUM — destructive calls fall back to the PRIMARY node when `Server.nodeId` is null

`prisma/schema.prisma:312` `nodeId String?` — nullable. `/opt/nxeon/lib/order.ts:174` can persist null: `nodeId = n?.id ?? null;`

Three identical fallbacks: `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:69-78`, `/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:37-61`, `/opt/nxeon/worker/disk-expand.ts:82-97` — all `server.node ?? primary ?? enabled`, then issue destroy/resize/disk-delete against `server.vmid` on *that* node.

**Failure scenario (multi-node):** server S lives on node B but has `nodeId = null`. Customer deletes a volume on S → `nodeFor` resolves node A → `conn.post(\`/nodes/A/qemu/${S.vmid}/config\`, { delete: "scsi1" })` → a **different customer's** VM on node A with the same vmid loses a disk. `Node` rows carry independent `apiUrl`s (`worker/volumes.ts:58`), so nothing guarantees vmid uniqueness across them. There is no `if (!server.nodeId) throw` gate on destructive job types.

### F9 — LOW/MEDIUM — worker handlers do zero re-validation

`/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:28-31`
```ts
const volume = await db.volume.findUnique({
  where: { id: payload.volumeId },
  include: { server: { include: { node: true } } },
});
```
No `userId`/`serverId` filter, and `worker/volumes.ts:15-17` states the design: *"Ownership + validation are enforced at enqueue time… so these handlers trust `payload.volumeId`."* Nothing asserts `volume.userId === volume.server.userId` before destroying a disk on that server. Not exploitable through the current enqueue paths (F-solid #6/#7 below), but any future code that can insert a `Job` row — an admin tool, the `lib/ai-build.ts`/`worker/claude.ts` surfaces, a manual SQL fix-up — gets an unauthenticated disk-destroy primitive.

### F10 — LOW — impersonation guard missing on volume spend + destroy; audit rows misattribute

`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-volumes.ts:3-8` never imports `assertNotImpersonating`, yet `:78` calls `debitWallet(tx, user.id, priceCents)`. `/opt/nxeon/lib/auth.ts:151` documents the rule: *"Call at the top of every spend path."* `lib/actions-disk.ts:42` complies; `actions-volumes.ts` does not.

Because `requireUser()` → `currentUser()` returns the **impersonated** user (`lib/auth.ts:92-111`), the audit rows at `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-volumes.ts:158-160` (`volume.detach`) and `:186-188` (`volume.delete`) record the *customer's* `userId` for an admin-initiated destruction. After a data-loss incident there is no record of who actually pressed the button.

---

## WHAT IS SOLID

**Shrink is genuinely impossible — four independent layers, all verified:**
1. `/opt/nxeon/lib/resize.ts:61-63` — `if (newPlan.diskGB < server.plan.diskGB) { throw new ResizeError("Disk storage can only grow — choose a plan with equal or larger disk."); }`
2. `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:163` — same check on the downgrade path, and the comment at `:159-162` correctly justifies comparing **plan** disks (extra is additive to both sides, so "new plan ≥ old plan" ⇔ "effective disk doesn't shrink"). The reasoning is right.
3. `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:552` — `if (newPlan.diskGB < server.plan.diskGB) throw new Error("resize: disk can only grow");` — **re-checked in the worker**, so a hand-crafted `RESIZE` job payload cannot shrink either.
4. `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:580` — the resize PUT is gated on `if (newTotalDiskGB > currentTotalDiskGB)`, so no shrink call is ever emitted.

**Client and server agree on the shrink basis** — no mismatch to exploit. `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx:604` passes `currentDiskGB={server.plan.diskGB}`, and `components/customer/ResizeDown.tsx:88` `const diskShrinks = p.diskGB < currentDiskGB;` compares exactly the quantity `resizeServerDown` compares. The greyed-out cards and the server guard cover the same set.

**`worker/disk-expand.ts` only ever emits a positive relative delta, computed from the live hypervisor state, not the DB** — `/opt/nxeon/worker/disk-expand.ts:340-347`:
```ts
const deltaGB = targetTotalGB - currentGB;
if (deltaGB > 0) {
  const upid = await conn.put(`/nodes/${conn.node}/qemu/${server.vmid}/resize`, {
    disk: "scsi0",
    size: `+${deltaGB}G`,
  });
```
with `currentGB` read from Proxmox at `:333-335`. A stale DB cannot produce a shrink here. (Minor hardening note: `worker/index.ts:583` sends an **absolute** `${newTotalDiskGB}G` instead — PVE rejects absolute shrinks server-side, so this is a hard-fail not a data loss, but the relative form in `disk-expand.ts` is the safer pattern and the two should match.)
